tools.name: compute_reinforced_soil_wall
tools.title: Compute Reinforced Soil Wall (RSW) BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_cantilever_wall. Reinforced soil retaining wall (RSW) using granular fill reinforced with horizontal layers of geogrid or steel tie strips, with one of four facing systems: precast concrete panels (Reinforced Earth™ / VSL Retained Earth style), segmental modular blocks (Allan Block / Keystone), wraparound soft face (vegetated or biodegradable mat), or Terramesh-style steel mesh face (re-using the S29 gabion vocabulary). The SECOND member of the earth_structures L1 leaf (after gabion_wall at S29), the SIXTH member of the wall family, the FIFTH structural system, and the FIRST wall family member with a face-area-primary measurement basis (m² of face + m² × layers of geogrid, both m²; every prior wall body was m³). 17th use of the classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern. Routes via four new WorkCategory entries (RSW_FACING_PANEL, RSW_MODULAR_BLOCK, RSW_WRAPAROUND_FACE, RSW_TIE_STRIP) plus the GEOGRID category (whose handler is gap-filled in CESMM4/NRM2/MMHW this session) plus re-use of GABION_BASKET on the STEEL_MESH_FACE variant. Codes: CESMM4 E.8.4-8 (Class E Earthworks §E.8 stabilisation), NRM2 5.23-27 (Group 5 Excavating and filling), MMHW 600.15-19 (Series 600 Earthworks; SHW Cl. 624 reinforced earth retaining structures), and SMM7 D41.3/D41.4/D41.5/D20.21/D20.14.2 (D41 — Crib walls / gabions / REINFORCED EARTH — the NAMED home, now serving TWO wall families). Eight variant presets exercise all four RSWFacing values (2/2/2/2 split). Example params: wall_height=6 m (0.5–12), wall_length=40 m (5–200), depth_into_fill_m=4.5 m (0.35–15). Example call: {"params": {"wall_height": 6, "wall_length": 40, "depth_into_fill_m": 4.5}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Parameter form for a reinforced soil wall.

A single dataclass that — through combinations of its fields and
the ``rsw_facing`` discriminator — produces all eight
VARIANT_PRESETS plus arbitrary user-specified geometries across
all four RSWFacing options. Sensible defaults yield a 6m
highway-approach PRECAST_PANEL wall.

rsw_facing.description:
Facing system of the reinforced soil wall.

PRECAST_PANEL   — Reinforced Earth™ / Freyssinet / VSL Retained Earth
                  style precast concrete facing panels (T-shape or
                  cruciform). Primary measurement: face area m²
                  routes to RSW_FACING_PANEL. Steel tie strips
                  route separately to RSW_TIE_STRIP. Geogrid
                  reinforcement (where used in addition to or in
                  place of tie strips) routes to GEOGRID. Typical
                  highway use: motorway widening, bridge approach
                  embankments, mainline-network junction
                  improvements.

MODULAR_BLOCK   — Segmental concrete block facing (Allan Block /
                  Keystone / Anchor / Versa-Lok). Primary
                  measurement: face area m² routes to
                  RSW_MODULAR_BLOCK. Geogrid layers clamped between
                  courses route to GEOGRID. Typical use: retail
                  park boundary walls, golf-course retaining walls,
                  cycle bridge approaches, residential development
                  grading.

WRAPAROUND      — Soft-faced wraparound system: geogrid wraps the
                  face of each lift and folds back into the
                  reinforced fill. Primary measurement: face area
                  m² routes to RSW_WRAPAROUND_FACE (the extra
                  wraparound geogrid is built into the rate);
                  horizontal reinforcement layers route to
                  GEOGRID. Typical use: embankment toe
                  stabilisation, slope-repair works, vegetated
                  landscape retaining structures, temporary
                  haul-road retaining walls.

STEEL_MESH_FACE — Welded steel mesh "gabion-style" face with
                  geogrid extending into the reinforced fill
                  behind (Maccaferri Terramesh / Tensar Terramesh
                  system). The face is structurally a gabion at
                  the face line but the bulk of the structure is
                  reinforced soil. Primary measurement: face is
                  a thin gabion-style basket and routes to
                  GABION_BASKET (re-using the S29 vocabulary —
                  every RSW STEEL_MESH_FACE variant has zero new
                  face WorkCategory introduction). Geogrid
                  reinforcement layers extending into the fill
                  route to GEOGRID. Typical use: highway boundary
                  walls where the gabion aesthetic is wanted but
                  the wall is too tall for a gravity gabion
                  structure.

geogrid_grade.description:
Geogrid product grade per BS EN 13251 / BS 8006-1:2010.

The grade governs the long-term design strength T_d (kN/m), which
drives the layer length and the layer count required for stability.

tools.name: compute_soil_nailed_slope
tools.title: Compute Soil-Nailed Slope BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_cantilever_wall. Cut slope stabilised by passively-stressed soil nails with an applied face system. Discriminates between four face systems via the face_system enum: SHOTCRETE_MESH (dominant UK highway-cutting choice per SHW Cl. 644), HARD_FACING_PANEL (premium permanent works), FLEXIBLE_MESH (weathered rock drape), and VEGETATED_GEOGRID (landscape-sensitive schemes). Third member of the earth_structures L1 leaf (after gabion_wall S29 and reinforced_soil_wall S30). Eight variant presets cover all four face systems × representative slope geometries. Routes via three new WorkCategory entries (SOIL_NAIL, SHOTCRETE_FACE, FACE_MESH_REINFORCEMENT) plus reuse of EXCAVATION_GENERAL, DISPOSAL, CONCRETE_REINFORCED, GEOTEXTILE_FILTER, GEOGRID, and TOPSOIL_PLACE. Codes: CESMM4 C.5.X (soil nail) + E.8.10 (shotcrete) + G.5.8 (mesh), NRM2 7.7.X + 5.28.1 + 11.6.1, MMHW 600.20.X + 600.21.1 + 600.22.1 (SHW Cl. 638-639 / Cl. 644), SMM7 D32.3.X (steel piling — soil nails) + D41.6/D41.7 (the NAMED home for the three earth-structures families now). 23rd use of the classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern; 4th use of the declared-then-banded pattern (nail_length_m bands the C.5.X / 7.7.X / 600.20.X / D32.3.X third digit). Example params: slope_height_m=8 m (0.5–25), slope_angle_deg=65 ° (10–89), slope_length_m=30 m (2–500). Example call: {"params": {"slope_height_m": 8, "slope_angle_deg": 65, "slope_length_m": 30}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Parameters for a single soil-nailed slope.

Geometry interpretation:
  - ``slope_height_m`` is the vertical extent of the cut slope
    (top of crest to toe of slope).
  - ``slope_angle_deg`` is the slope angle from horizontal
    (typically 50-80° for soil-nailed cuts).
  - ``slope_length_m`` is the horizontal length along the slope
    crest — the spatial extent of the assembly along the highway
    alignment.
  - ``nail_rows`` is the number of horizontal rows of nails;
    ``nail_horizontal_spacing_m`` and ``nail_vertical_spacing_m``
    give the in-row and between-row centres (m).
  - ``nail_length_m`` is the design nail length (excavation +
    bond length; same for all nails in this assembly — for
    variable-length schemes, instantiate multiple assemblies).
  - ``nail_inclination_deg`` is the angle below horizontal of
    the nail axis (typically 10-20°).

Face-system attributes (used only if relevant to ``face_system``):
  - ``shotcrete_thickness_mm`` / ``shotcrete_grade`` / 
    ``face_mesh_designation`` — SHOTCRETE_MESH only.
  - ``panel_thickness_mm`` / ``panel_concrete_grade`` —
    HARD_FACING_PANEL only.
  - ``geogrid_grade`` / ``topsoil_thickness_mm`` —
    VEGETATED_GEOGRID only.

face_system.description:
Face system for the soil-nailed slope.

SHOTCRETE_MESH    — Wet-mix sprayed concrete (typically C25/30 to
                    C32/40) over a single layer of welded steel
                    fabric mesh (BS 4483 A193 to A393), with
                    horizontal reinforcing waling bars at each
                    nail row. The dominant UK choice for permanent
                    highway-cutting stabilisation per SHW Cl. 644.
                    Routes: SHOTCRETE_FACE (m²) + FACE_MESH_
                    REINFORCEMENT (m²) + SOIL_NAIL (Nr) +
                    GEOTEXTILE_FILTER (m², drainage strips).

HARD_FACING_PANEL — Precast concrete face panels (typically 1.5m
                    × 1.5m × 0.15m thick, RC) bolted to the slope
                    via the nail head plates. The premium face
                    system for permanent works adjacent to
                    sensitive receptors (carriageways, railways,
                    bridges) where the maintained appearance of a
                    hard concrete face is required and the
                    durability requirement exceeds shotcrete's
                    design life. Routes: CONCRETE_REINFORCED
                    (m³, panels) + SOIL_NAIL (Nr) +
                    GEOTEXTILE_FILTER (m²). NB: shotcrete and
                    face mesh are NOT emitted — the precast
                    panel IS the face.

FLEXIBLE_MESH     — Heavy-duty galvanised steel mesh drape (BS 4483
                    A252 or similar, but typically a proprietary
                    rockfall/erosion-protection drape mesh such as
                    Geobrugg TECCO, Maccaferri Steelgrid HR) over
                    the slope face, pinned by the nail head plates
                    but NOT covered by shotcrete. The light-touch
                    face system for weathered-rock cut faces where
                    the dominant failure mode is surface ravelling
                    rather than mass instability. Routes:
                    FACE_MESH_REINFORCEMENT (m²) + SOIL_NAIL (Nr).
                    No shotcrete, no drainage strips required.

VEGETATED_GEOGRID — Geogrid (PP or HDPE biaxial, e.g. Tensar SS35
                    or Maccaferri PSG type) wrapped over the
                    slope face with topsoil and seed/turf
                    established on the surface. The soft-face,
                    environmentally-sensitive option — used for
                    landslide stabilisation in rural / parkland
                    settings, river-bank stabilisation, and
                    landscape-led highway schemes. Routes:
                    GEOGRID (m²) + SOIL_NAIL (Nr) + GEOTEXTILE_
                    FILTER (m², drainage strips) + TOPSOIL_PLACE
                    (m², face soil layer).

The four face systems span UK practice from light protection
(FLEXIBLE_MESH) through standard (SHOTCRETE_MESH) and premium
(HARD_FACING_PANEL) to environmentally-sensitive (VEGETATED_
GEOGRID). These are the genuinely different commercial
decision points a QS would face when pricing a soil-nailed
slope tender.

nail_permanence.description:
Permanent or temporary soil nail per BS EN 14490 Table 1.

PERMANENT — Design life ≥ 2 years. Bar requires double corrosion
            protection (DCP): epoxy-coated bar OR galvanised bar
            + grouted cementitious annulus + corrugated plastic
            sheath. Conventional UK choice for highway-cutting
            stabilisation under SHW Cl. 644.
TEMPORARY — Design life < 2 years. Single corrosion protection
            (SCP) acceptable — bare bar in cementitious grout
            annulus is sufficient. Used for temporary basement
            support and short-term construction-phase
            stabilisation.

Wire shape is a flat object (`{"concrete_m3": {...}, "rebar_t": {...}}`).

surface uniform with the rest of this module.

anyOf.description:

drawing both tiers see in the workspace, surfaced on the MCP compute
response so a chat client can render it inline (60th-fire item C). This
is the on-screen preview — present on BOTH tiers per the free/paid
boundary; the downloadable CAD artefacts (DXF / dimensioned PDF) remain
the paid differentiator via the export tools.

tools.name: compute_embankment_cross_section
tools.title: Compute Embankment Cross-Section BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Geometry-driven embankment per MMHW Series 600 — trapezoidal cross-section with crest width, asymmetric side slopes (h:v), and per-chainage height profile. Auto-generates the CrossSection series and delegates volume integration + mass-haul + standards routing to the end_area_earthworks engine, inheriting the four-standard rendering invariant. Auto-computes topsoil strip footprint from toe-to-toe envelope and supports an optional founding-strip excavation below ground level. Example params: crest_width_m=10 m (3–30), side_slope_h_per_v=2 (1–4), strip_envelope_offset_m=0.5 m (0–2). Example call: {"params": {"crest_width_m": 10, "side_slope_h_per_v": 2, "strip_envelope_offset_m": 0.5}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Inputs for a geometry-driven embankment cross-section assembly.

The assembly generates a `CrossSection` list from the profile +
geometry parameters, builds an `EndAreaEarthworksParameters` from
the result + the material/method parameters carried here, and
delegates compute to `EndAreaEarthworks.compute(...)`.

Per Session 12 Q2 decision: left and right slopes are exposed
separately, both defaulting to `side_slope_h_per_v` so the common
symmetric case is a single-parameter call.

items.description:
A single point on the embankment height profile.

`height_m` is the embankment height above the existing ground at this
chainage. Zero means the embankment has zero height (the alignment
has reached existing ground level — the embankment toe).

method.description:
Integration method preference. The actual method applied may
differ — see VolumeResult.method_used.

cut_class.description:
Full SHW Series 600 Table 6/1 acceptable material class set, plus the
Table 6/2 unacceptable classes.

The enum value is the SHW designator. Use `family` and `default_use`
properties for routing in the assembly and renderer code.

fill_class.description:
Full SHW Series 600 Table 6/1 acceptable material class set, plus the
Table 6/2 unacceptable classes.

The enum value is the SHW designator. Use `family` and `default_use`
properties for routing in the assembly and renderer code.

The enum value is the SHW designator. Use `family` and `default_use`

anyOf.description:
SHW Series 600 Cl. 605 bulking/shrinkage factors.

bulk_factor — multiplier applied to the in-situ cut volume to get
              the loose volume that needs haulage. Typical values:
                1.10 for granular (Class 1x)
                1.20 for cohesive (Class 2x)
                1.30 for chalk (Class 3)
                1.50 for rock (Class 8)
              Default = 1.20 (conservative average for mixed cut).
shrink_factor — multiplier applied to the in-situ fill volume to
              get the volume of cut required to produce it.
              Typical values:
                0.95 for granular
                0.85 for cohesive
                0.80 for stabilised
              Default = 0.90 (conservative average for mixed fill).

tools.name: compute_end_area_earthworks
tools.title: Compute End-Area Earthworks BoQ
tools.description: Free tier. Renders the MMHW standard only — CESMM4, NRM2 and SMM7 require a paid tier. Anonymous callers welcome. Linear earthworks reach measured by the end-area method per MMHW Series 600 — Simpson's Rule with UK-QS even-ordinate trapezoidal-boundary fallback, with full SHW Series 600 Table 6/1 class tagging, mass-haul diagram (bulking + shrinkage per SHW Cl. 605), cut/fill balance, DISPOSAL vs FILL_GENERAL routing, capping and sub-base build-up, and topsoil strip + replacement. Renders identically across CESMM4 / NRM2 / MMHW / SMM7 with per-class line distinction. Example params: unacceptable_proportion=0 (0–1), topsoil_strip_depth_m=0.15 m (0–1), topsoil_replace_depth_mm=150 mm (0–500). Example call: {"params": {"unacceptable_proportion": 0, "topsoil_strip_depth_m": 0.15, "topsoil_replace_depth_mm": 150}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Inputs for a linear earthworks reach measured by the end-area method.

The five area streams in each `CrossSection` are integrated independently
along the chainage axis. `topsoil_strip_area` is the planar (m²)
strip area at each section; the volume is computed as
`trap-integrate(topsoil_strip_area) × topsoil_strip_depth_m / strip_area_mean`
— i.e. we multiply the integrated planar strip area by the strip depth
to get a volume in m³. Conventionally `topsoil_strip_area` per the
designer is planar in m² per running metre (m² of plan area per metre
of chainage = m of width), but to keep CrossSection symmetric with the
other four area streams we treat it as a true area (m²) at that station
and apply the depth multiplication here.

items.description:
A single surveyed cross-section at a known chainage.

All areas are in m² (the planar cross-section area). The chainage
is in m along the centreline.

The optional `notes` field carries any inspector commentary that
should appear in the audit trail (e.g. "soft spot, U2 material
expected below formation"). The optional `attributes` carries any
further structured data that downstream consumers may want (per-class
cut splits, designer's identifier, etc.).

anyOf.description:
SHW Series 600 Cl. 605 bulking/shrinkage factors.

bulk_factor — multiplier applied to the in-situ cut volume to get
              the loose volume that needs haulage. Typical values:
                1.10 for granular (Class 1x)
                1.20 for cohesive (Class 2x)
                1.30 for chalk (Class 3)
                1.50 for rock (Class 8)
              Default = 1.20 (conservative average for mixed cut).

              get the volume of cut required to produce it.
              Typical values:
                0.95 for granular
                0.85 for cohesive
                0.80 for stabilised
              Default = 0.90 (conservative average for mixed fill).

tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Bridge / structural-deck parapet installation per BS 6779-1 + BS EN 1317-2 + SHW Cl. 408. Discriminates between four UK parapet system classifications via the parapet_type enum (pedestrian_only per BS 7818; vehicle_p1_p2 — low-containment BS EN 1317-2; vehicle_h1_h2_h3 — higher-containment; combined_pedestrian_vehicle — composite design). Plus parallel discriminators on two further WorkCategory entries: same parapet_type on PARAPET_POST, transition_type on PARAPET_TRANSITION (to_vrs / to_abutment / expansion_joint). The MMHW Series 400 _parapet handler is the platform's SEVENTH 1D-banded handler — code `400.4.1.{c}` bands by containment_level (4 bands per BS EN 1317-2). 1D choice is disciplined — second principled rejection of forced 2D banding (after S38 road_marking). LAUNCH-COMPLETING 45TH ASSEMBLY — opens highway_bridge_edge L2 leaf, closing the highway suite at 5/5 populated leaves and the platform at 45/45 launch target. SMM7 routes BACK to Q40 (sibling slot to VRS at Q40.5) — preserves UK trade reality. Example params: parapet_height_mm=1100 mm (900–1800), parapet_length_m=25 m (1–2000), post_count=0 Nr (0–200). Example call: {"params": {"parapet_height_mm": 1100, "parapet_length_m": 25, "post_count": 0}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Inputs for the parapet assembly.

Required:
  parapet_type        — ParapetType enum (or string equivalent)
  containment_level   — ContainmentLevel enum (or string)
  parapet_height_mm   — nominal parapet height above deck in mm
  parapet_length_m    — parapet run length in metres

Optional:
  post_count          — number of enumerated posts (default 0 —
                        posts deemed-included in parapet m-rate).
                        Set > 0 only for contracts requiring
                        specialist per-post pricing.
  transition_type     — TransitionType enum (or string). Required
                        if transition_count > 0.
  transition_count    — number of transition pieces (default 0).

parapet_type.description:
Parapet system classification per UK design practice.

PEDESTRIAN_ONLY              — BS 7818 handrail-and-infill for
    footway / pedestrian-only bridges. Live load to BS EN 1991-2
    but NO vehicle containment requirement.
VEHICLE_P1_P2                — BS EN 1317-2 containment class P1
    or P2. Low-containment vehicle parapet for low-speed roads
    (≤50mph). NOTE: in BS EN 1317-2 itself, P1/P2 are pedestrian
    classes; UK vehicle-parapet practice extends the P-prefix to
    cover low-containment vehicle situations.
VEHICLE_H1_H2_H3             — BS EN 1317-2 containment class H1,
    H2 or H3. Higher-containment vehicle parapet for motorways
    and high-speed roads.
COMBINED_PEDESTRIAN_VEHICLE  — Composite design with vehicle-rated
    lower section per BS EN 1317-2 and pedestrian-rated upper rail
    per BS 7818. Used on shared footway/carriageway bridges.

containment_level.description:
BS EN 1317-2 / BS EN 1317-6 containment classification.

Pedestrian classes:
  P1 — Light pedestrian containment.
  P2 — Heavier pedestrian containment (e.g. cyclist permitted).

Vehicle classes (ascending containment energy):
  N1 — Low containment, normal traffic.
  N2 — Higher of the normal range.
  H1 — Higher containment, high-speed road.
  H2 — Higher containment, dual carriageway.
  H3 — Very high containment, motorway.
  H4a — Highest containment, motorway HGV restraint.
  H4b — Highest containment, motorway HGV+bus restraint.

anyOf.description:
Parapet transition classification.

TO_VRS          — Most common. Parapet-to-ground-level VRS
    transition at the bridge approach end (deck-end to embankment).
    Subject to BS EN 1317-4 transition compatibility requirements.
TO_ABUTMENT     — Parapet anchorage transition into masonry or
    concrete bridge abutment wall (no VRS continuation —
    terminates at the abutment).
EXPANSION_JOINT — Continuity break in the parapet at a deck
    expansion joint on long bridges, accommodating structural
    movement.

tools.name: compute_highway_drainage_channel
tools.title: Compute Highway Drainage Channel BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Highway / surface-water drainage channel installation per BS EN 1433 + SHW Cl. 511-514 + HD 33/16. Discriminates between five UK channel product classifications via the channel_type enum (linear_polymer_concrete — ACO-pattern; linear_concrete — Charcon-pattern precast; slot_drain — narrow-slot recessed; combined_kerb_drainage — Beany/Safeticurb integrated unit per SHW Cl. 514; steel_grated_channel — heavy-duty stainless/galvanised). Plus parallel discriminators on two further WorkCategory entries: outfall_type on CHANNEL_OUTFALL (end / branch / side), silt_box_type on CHANNEL_SILT_BOX (standard / heavy-duty / deep-sump). The MMHW Series 500 _highway_drainage_channel handler is the platform's FOURTH 2D-banded handler — code `500.8.{t}.{d}` bands by channel_type (5 bands) AND depth_class (4 bands). 5×4 = 20-cell grid. SMM7 routes to R12 (Drainage below ground) — SECOND highway L1 family outside Section Q after S39 lighting → V41. Example params: channel_depth_mm=100 mm (50–1500), channel_length_m=50 m (1–500), outfall_count=1 nr (0–20). Example call: {"params": {"channel_depth_mm": 100, "channel_length_m": 50, "outfall_count": 1}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Inputs for the highway_drainage_channel assembly.

Required:
  channel_type           — ChannelType enum (or string equivalent)
  depth_class            — DepthClass enum (or string)
  channel_depth_mm       — actual channel depth in mm
  channel_length_m       — channel run length in metres

Optional:
  outfall_type           — OutfallType enum (or string); defaults to
                           END_OUTFALL when outfall_count > 0
  outfall_count          — number of primary outfalls (default 1)
  branch_outfall_count   — number of additional branch outfalls
                           (default 0)
  silt_box_type          — SiltBoxType enum (or string); required
                           when silt_box_count > 0
  silt_box_count         — number of silt boxes (default 0)

channel_type.description:
Channel product classification per BS EN 1433 + UK industry practice.

LINEAR_POLYMER_CONCRETE — Monolithic moulded fibre-reinforced polymer-
    concrete unit (ACO-pattern, the dominant UK case). Tight-tolerance
    manufactured joint, ductile-iron grating per BS EN 124.
LINEAR_CONCRETE         — Precast reinforced concrete unit (Charcon-
    pattern). Rebated joint, ductile-iron grating per BS EN 124.
SLOT_DRAIN              — Recessed narrow-slot channel section
    (stainless-steel or polymer-concrete). Used where visual
    impact must be minimised (conservation areas, pedestrianised
    zones, courtyard schemes).
COMBINED_KERB_DRAINAGE  — Integrated kerb+drain monolithic unit per
    SHW Cl. 514 (Beany / Safeticurb-pattern). The kerb face and
    the channel are a single precast item. Used where kerb-line
    installation and surface drainage are integrated.
STEEL_GRATED_CHANNEL    — Heavy-duty stainless-steel or galvanised-
    steel grated channel for industrial-loading service
    (Class E600/F900 BS EN 124). Used at airports, port hardstandings,
    and industrial yards.

depth_class.description:
Channel depth classification per typical UK pricing tiers.

Depth drives unit weight, bedding volume, trench-support
requirement, and ground-water-handling cost independently of the
channel type. UK practice prices channel depth in four
commercial bands:

SHALLOW    — ≤150mm. Footway / pedestrian area / car park.
MEDIUM     — 151-300mm. Standard carriageway edge.
DEEP       — 301-500mm. High-flow carriageway / motorway edge.
EXTRA_DEEP — >500mm. Junction sump / heavy-flow location.

anyOf.description:
Outfall fitting classification per UK industry practice.

END_OUTFALL    — Termination of channel run with downstream
    connection to chamber or carrier pipe.
BRANCH_OUTFALL — Mid-run discharge connection (T-fitting to
    the channel base).
SIDE_OUTFALL   — Lateral discharge to an adjacent chamber
    (S-fitting through the channel side wall).

Silt box classification per BS EN 124 load class + service.

STANDARD   — Class C250 BS EN 124. Footway / car park service.
HEAVY_DUTY — Class D400 BS EN 124. Standard carriageway service.
DEEP_SUMP  — Extended sediment trap depth. For high-silt-load
    locations (forest edge, construction-site adjacent, etc.).

tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Highway / street lighting column installation per BS EN 40 + BS 5489-1:2020 + TR 22. Discriminates between four UK column material classifications via the column_type enum (steel_galvanised, aluminium, composite_grp, decorative_cast_iron). Plus parallel discriminators on three further WorkCategory entries: foundation_type on COLUMN_FOUNDATION, luminaire_type on LUMINAIRE, bracket_type on COLUMN_BRACKET. The MMHW Series 1300 _lighting_column handler is the platform's THIRD 2D-banded handler — code `1300.4.1.{h}.{c}` bands by column_height_class (6 bands per TR 22) AND column_loading_class (4 bands per BS EN 40-3). 6×4 = 24-cell grid (the LARGEST banded grid in the platform). Example params: mounting_height_m=6 m (4–16), luminaire_wattage_W=60 W (10–1000), bracket_count=0 Nr (0–4). Example call: {"params": {"mounting_height_m": 6, "luminaire_wattage_W": 60, "bracket_count": 0}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Inputs for the lighting_column assembly.

Defaults anchored to URBAN_6M_LED — UK urban distributor: 6 m steel
galvanised column on precast socket, BS EN 40-3 Class B, LED M-class
luminaire (~60 W typical). Required-field defaults added per G.6.7.24
precedent — non-breaking API enrichment opens the slug to schema-
driven workspace defaults.

column_type.description:
Column material classification per BS EN 40-5/6/7.

STEEL_GALVANISED — Carbon-steel column shaft, hot-dip galvanised
    after fabrication. The dominant UK case (~85% of new street
    lighting installations). BS EN 40-5.
ALUMINIUM        — Extruded aluminium column. Used for ped-cycle
    track lighting (lighter handling) and seafront/marine zones
    (corrosion resistance). BS EN 40-6.
COMPOSITE_GRP    — Glass-reinforced polymer column. Used in zones
    with high crash energy (frangible) or where electrical
    isolation is required. BS EN 40-7.
DECORATIVE_CAST_IRON — Cast-iron decorative column for conservation
    areas and heritage zones. Bespoke finish; BS EN 40-5 with
    traditional Victorian/Edwardian design.

column_height_class.description:
Column mounting height class per TR 22 standard heights.

The six values correspond to UK standard heights for street
lighting. Each height class drives steel section thickness, base
plate size, and foundation depth per BS EN 40-2.

H_5M  — 5m  (residential / footway side)
H_6M  — 6m  (urban residential / pedestrian areas)
H_8M  — 8m  (urban distributor / town centre)
H_10M — 10m (urban traffic route / arterial)
H_12M — 12m (motorway slip road / interchange approaches)
H_15M — 15m (motorway main line / high-mast areas)

column_loading_class.description:
Column wind-loading class per BS EN 40-3.

The class defines the permitted luminaire+bracket projected wind
area for a given column section. Class jumps drive the column's
steel weight independently of mounting height.

A — small luminaire, projected area <0.025 m²
B — medium luminaire, 0.025-0.045 m²
C — large luminaire / single bracket, 0.045-0.075 m²
D — high-mast / multi-luminaire, >0.075 m²

foundation_type.description:
Column foundation classification per SHW Cl. 1304 / TR 22.

PRECAST_SOCKET     — Precast concrete plant base socket. Typical
    for columns ≤8m on residential/urban streets. Quick install
    (drop-in), reusable across the contractor's stock.
INSITU_REINFORCED  — In-situ reinforced concrete foundation with
    holding-down bolts. Typical for columns ≥10m where wind/dynamic
    loads exceed the precast socket's anchorage capacity.
ROOT_PLANTED       — Direct-buried planted column (no separate
    foundation block); the steel column extends below ground to
    TR 22 minimum embedment depth.

luminaire_type.description:
Luminaire classification per BS EN 13201 / ILP TR23.

LED_M_CLASS    — LED luminaire suitable for M-class carriageway
    lighting per BS EN 13201. The dominant new-install case
    post-2015.
LED_DECORATIVE — LED decorative lantern for conservation-area /
    heritage zones (Victorian/Edwardian styling).
SON_LEGACY     — High-pressure sodium SON lamp luminaire. Legacy
    only — included for like-for-like replacement schemes.
SOX_LEGACY     — Low-pressure sodium SOX lamp luminaire. Legacy
    only — banned for new installs since the 2010s; included for
    rare replacement.
FLOODLIGHT     — Asymmetric-beam floodlight luminaire (junction
    floodlighting, pedestrian-area floodlighting).

anyOf.description:
Column bracket classification per BS EN 40-2.

SINGLE_SIDE_ENTRY     — Single side-entry outreach bracket. The
    dominant case for carriageway lighting where the luminaire
    is offset over the kerb.
DOUBLE_SIDE_ENTRY     — Double side-entry bracket carrying two
    luminaires (one each side). Used at junctions / where dual
    carriageways meet at a single column.
POST_TOP_ADAPTOR      — Post-top adaptor (luminaire mounted on
    column tip, no outreach). Used for residential and ped-cycle
    lighting where the luminaire is directly above the column.
DECORATIVE_SWAN_NECK   — Decorative swan-neck bracket for heritage
    / conservation zones.

tools.name: compute_vehicle_restraint_system
tools.title: Compute Vehicle Restraint System (VRS) BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Vehicle restraint system (VRS) for highway works per SHW Cl. 401-419 and BS EN 1317. Discriminates between six structural system types via the vrs_system_type enum: tensioned and untensioned corrugated steel beam, wire rope, in-situ concrete step barrier, precast concrete single-slope, and combined heavy-duty (corrugated beam over concrete kerb upstand). FIRST member of the highway_restraint L2 leaf — opens the brand-new highway L1 category as the 40th assembly. Six variant presets cover the principal UK commercial scenarios: motorway verge TCB N2/W4, motorway central wire rope N2/W6, urban untensioned N2/W2, bridge approach concrete step H2/W1, median precast single-slope H2/W2, and high-containment verge H4a/W4. Routes via three new WorkCategory entries (VEHICLE_RESTRAINT_SYSTEM, VRS_TERMINAL, VRS_TRANSITION) plus reuse of CONCRETE_REINFORCED, REINFORCEMENT, FORMWORK and EXCAVATION_TRENCH for the concrete variants. Codes: CESMM4 X.3 (Class X §3 — crash barriers), NRM2 34.7 (Site works — crash barriers), MMHW 400.1.{ww}.{cl} (Series 400 — Road Restraint Systems, with 2D banding by working_width × containment), SMM7 Q40.5 (Section Q40 — Fencing, crash barriers). 24th use of the classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern; 5th use of the declared-then-banded pattern AND the FIRST 2D-banded handler (MMHW 400.1.{ww}.{cl} bands by both axes simultaneously). Example params: length_m=100 m (12–10000), post_spacing_m=2 m (0.5–8), foundation_width_m=0.9 m (0.2–2). Example call: {"params": {"length_m": 100, "post_spacing_m": 2, "foundation_width_m": 0.9}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Parameters for a single vehicle restraint system run.

Geometry interpretation:
  - ``length_m`` is the run length along the highway alignment.
  - ``post_spacing_m`` is the centre-to-centre spacing of supporting
    steel posts (irrelevant for INSITU and PRECAST_SLAB foundation
    types). Typical UK values: 2.0m (TCB), 4.0m (TCB W6 variant),
    3.2m (wire rope), 1.5m (high-containment hybrid).
  - ``terminals_per_run`` is typically 2 (one at each end of a
    continuous run); can be 1 for a barrier that returns into a
    structure at one end.
  - ``transitions`` is the number of system-type transitions
    within the run (e.g. to a parapet or to a different VRS type).
    Zero is normal for a single-system run.

System-type-specific attributes (set only those relevant to the
variant's ``vrs_system_type``):
  - ``beam_thickness_mm`` — corrugated-beam variants only.
  - ``wire_strands`` / ``wire_tension_kn`` — wire rope only.
  - ``concrete_grade`` / ``concrete_cross_section_m2`` /
    ``reinforcement_kg_per_m`` — concrete variants only.
  - ``foundation_width_m`` / ``foundation_depth_m`` — INSITU_FOUND
    foundation only.
  - ``precast_unit_length_m`` — precast variants only.

vrs_system_type.description:
Vehicle restraint system structural type per BS EN 1317-2 / SHW
Cl. 402-404.

TENSIONED_CORRUGATED_BEAM   — Hot-dip galvanised steel "W-beam"
    section, tensioned end-to-end via anchor terminals. Steel posts
    at 2.0m or 4.0m centres (driven or socketed). The dominant UK
    motorway-verge system per SHW Cl. 402 Working Width 4 (W4)
    Containment N2. Single-sided.

UNTENSIONED_CORRUGATED_BEAM — Same W-beam profile but without
    end-anchored tensioning — relies on post stiffness rather than
    cable tension. Lower containment, higher working width. SHW
    Cl. 402 Working Width 2 (W2) Containment N2. Used on urban
    dual-carriageways and where containment requirement is
    moderate.

WIRE_ROPE                   — 3- or 4-strand pre-tensioned steel
    wire rope between sparse posts (3.2m centres typical). Highest
    working width for given containment (W6 or higher), narrowest
    physical footprint. The dominant UK motorway-central-reserve
    system per SHW Cl. 403. NOT permitted in narrow central
    reserves where W6 cannot be accommodated.

CONCRETE_STEP_INSITU        — In-situ reinforced concrete VRS,
    F-shape or step-shape cross-section per SHW Cl. 404. Highest
    containment per UK practice (H2 standard, H4a for vulnerable-
    receptor verges). Working width W1-W2. The dominant UK choice
    for bridge approaches, viaduct edges, and verges adjacent to
    watercourses/structures. Carries BS 8666 reinforcement.

CONCRETE_SINGLE_SLOPE_PRECAST — Precast concrete F-shape units
    (typically 6m units, bolted to slab foundation or sit-on-grade).
    Same containment family as CONCRETE_STEP_INSITU but priced as
    precast supply-and-install. Reinforcement deemed-included in
    the precast unit price. Used where rapid installation is
    commercially decisive (rolling roadworks, off-peak working).

COMBINED_HEAVY_DUTY         — Tensioned corrugated beam over a
    concrete kerb upstand or with double-rail layout for H4a
    containment. SHW Cl. 402 + Cl. 404 hybrid. Used at the
    outboard side of motorway verges adjacent to schools,
    residential properties, or sensitive natural features where
    H4a containment is the design requirement.

The six system types span the genuinely-different UK commercial
decisions a QS would face when pricing a VRS tender.

working_width_class.description:
BS EN 1317-2 working width class. The maximum lateral
displacement of the barrier under design impact, measured in metres.
UK practice typically specifies one of these four classes:

W1  — ≤ 0.6m  (minimum footprint, concrete VRS only)
W2  — ≤ 0.8m  (concrete VRS, untensioned corrugated, narrow median)
W4  — ≤ 1.3m  (tensioned corrugated beam typical)
W6  — ≤ 2.1m  (wire rope typical)

containment_level.description:
BS EN 1317-2 containment level. The vehicle mass + speed test
class the barrier has been demonstrated to contain. UK practice
typically specifies one of:

N2  — Normal containment (passenger car, 1500kg @ 110km/h)
H1  — Higher containment 1 (rigid heavy vehicle, 10000kg @ 70km/h)
H2  — Higher containment 2 (single-deck bus, 13000kg @ 70km/h)
H4a — Highest containment (rigid lorry, 30000kg @ 65km/h)

foundation_type.description:
Post/barrier foundation type. Drives whether excavation and
concrete foundation lines are emitted.

DRIVEN        — Steel post driven directly into the verge.
                No excavation or concrete foundation emitted.
                Conventional for TENSIONED_CORRUGATED_BEAM and
                UNTENSIONED_CORRUGATED_BEAM on standard verges.

SOCKETED      — Steel post set into a precast concrete socket;
                socket embedded in lean-mix concrete foundation.
                Emits a concrete foundation line (m³). Used where
                driven installation is not feasible (rock close to
                surface, contaminated ground, sensitive utilities).

INSITU_FOUND  — Continuous reinforced concrete strip foundation
                cast beneath in-situ concrete VRS. Emits
                CONCRETE_REINFORCED + REINFORCEMENT + FORMWORK
                lines for the foundation itself. Always paired
                with CONCRETE_STEP_INSITU.

PRECAST_SLAB  — Precast concrete VRS units sit on a pre-cast
                levelled slab foundation; foundation deemed
                included in the precast supply rate.

terminal_class.description:
BS EN 1317-4 terminal performance class. P1-P4 reflects energy
absorption and lateral redirection performance under impact.
Higher number = more demanding test.

tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Road marking installation per SHW Cl. 1207-1215 and TSRGD 2016. Discriminates between five UK marking-line classifications via the marking_line_type enum: continuous, broken_short, broken_long, double_continuous, lane_line. Plus parallel discriminators on three further WorkCategory entries: area_marking_type on ROAD_MARKING_AREA, symbol_type on ROAD_MARKING_SYMBOL, and stud_type on ROAD_STUD. THIRD member of the highway L1 leaf (after S36 VRS, S37 traffic_sign) and SECOND member of the highway_signs_markings L2 leaf — 42nd assembly. The highway_signs_markings L2 leaf becomes the first L2 leaf in the highway L1 to reach 2 members. Five variant presets cover the principal UK commercial scenarios: urban continuous white line, rural broken centreline with hazard, motorway hatched chevron, junction give-way with triangle, and motorway lane line with studs. Routes via four new WorkCategory entries (ROAD_MARKING_LINE, ROAD_MARKING_AREA, ROAD_MARKING_SYMBOL, ROAD_STUD). Codes: CESMM4 X.5 (Class X §5 — road markings), NRM2 34.9 (Site works — markings), MMHW 1200.1.{w} (Series 1200 — Traffic Signs and Road Markings, with 1D banding by line_width_class), SMM7 Q40.7 (Section Q40 — Fencing/site furniture). 26th use of classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern; 7th use of declared-then-banded (remains 1D — material rejected as a banding axis). Broadest unit-mix in any single CivilQuants assembly: m of line + m² of area + nr of symbol + nr of stud. Example params: actual_line_width_mm=100 mm (50–450), line_length_m=200 m (0–10000), secondary_line_length_m=0 m (0–10000). Example call: {"params": {"actual_line_width_mm": 100, "line_length_m": 200, "secondary_line_length_m": 0}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Parameters for a single road marking installation.

Defaults anchored to URBAN_CONTINUOUS_WHITE_LINE — 200 m of
continuous 100 mm thermoplastic edge/centre line. Required-field
defaults added per G.6.7.24 precedent — non-breaking API enrichment
opens the slug to schema-driven workspace defaults and defaults-
based parity-fixture regen.

Geometry interpretation:
  - ``line_length_m`` is the linear length of the primary marking
    line (continuous edge/centre line, broken pattern, etc.). UK
    practice measures along the line centreline. Set to 0 if no
    primary line is part of the installation.
  - ``secondary_line_length_m`` is for installations with two distinct
    line types (e.g. broken_short main centreline + broken_long
    hazard section). Set to 0 to omit. The secondary line shares
    the same width_class and material as the primary line.
  - ``area_m2`` is the m² of painted area marking (hatched chevron,
    ghost island, box junction, etc.). Set to 0 if no area is
    present.
  - ``symbol_count`` is the number of distinct painted symbol
    occurrences (arrows, words, give-way triangles). Set to 0 if
    no symbols are present.
  - ``stud_count`` is the number of reflective road studs. Set to
    0 if no studs are present.

Discrimination & banding:
  - ``marking_line_type`` discriminates the description text for the
    ROAD_MARKING_LINE WorkItem(s). Required if line_length_m > 0.
  - ``line_width_class`` discriminates the BANDED CODE in MMHW
    (1D-banding axis) and the description text in other standards.
  - ``area_marking_type`` discriminates description for the
    ROAD_MARKING_AREA WorkItem. Required if area_m2 > 0.
  - ``symbol_type`` discriminates description for the
    ROAD_MARKING_SYMBOL WorkItem. Required if symbol_count > 0.
  - ``stud_type`` and ``reflective_colour`` discriminate description
    for the ROAD_STUD WorkItem. Required if stud_count > 0.
  - ``marking_material`` is carried on every description but is
    NOT a discriminator or banding axis (UK QS convention).

anyOf.description:
Longitudinal road marking line type per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 6.

CONTINUOUS — Continuous longitudinal line. Used for edge lines, lane
    edge lines on motorways, and prohibitive centre lines where
    overtaking is forbidden. The dominant single-line case.

BROKEN_SHORT — Broken short-pattern line (short mark, long gap).
    Used for permissive centre lines on rural roads and lane lines
    on dual carriageways. Standard pattern per TSRGD diagram 1004.

BROKEN_LONG — Broken long-pattern hazard warning line (long mark,
    short gap). Used for cautionary centre lines warning of hazard
    ahead — junction approach, bend ahead, restricted visibility.
    TSRGD diagram 1005.

DOUBLE_CONTINUOUS — Double continuous longitudinal line, used where
    overtaking is prohibited in both directions. TSRGD diagram
    1013.1.

LANE_LINE — Lane-dividing line on motorway or dual-carriageway
    (broken pattern, typically 100mm with reflective studs).
    TSRGD diagram 1004.

The five line types span the genuinely-different UK commercial
decisions a QS would face when pricing a road-marking tender.

line_width_class.description:
Line width band per UK QS pricing practice. Line width is the
dominant cost driver per linear metre of marking — paint coverage
scales linearly with width, and the marking-application contractor
prices per width band.

STANDARD_100MM     — ≤150mm (standard centre/edge line; 100mm is
                     the dominant case)
WIDE_200MM         — >150-200mm (motorway edge line, distributor-
                     road edge line)
EXTRA_WIDE_300MM   — >200-300mm (stop line at signalised junction,
                     heavy-use edge line)
HATCHED_400MM_PLUS — >300mm (hatched edge stripe, ghost-island
                     boundary marking)

anyOf.description:
Longitudinal road marking line type per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 6.

CONTINUOUS — Continuous longitudinal line. Used for edge lines, lane
    edge lines on motorways, and prohibitive centre lines where
    overtaking is forbidden. The dominant single-line case.

BROKEN_SHORT — Broken short-pattern line (short mark, long gap).
    Used for permissive centre lines on rural roads and lane lines
    on dual carriageways. Standard pattern per TSRGD diagram 1004.

BROKEN_LONG — Broken long-pattern hazard warning line (long mark,
    short gap). Used for cautionary centre lines warning of hazard
    ahead — junction approach, bend ahead, restricted visibility.
    TSRGD diagram 1005.

DOUBLE_CONTINUOUS — Double continuous longitudinal line, used where
    overtaking is prohibited in both directions. TSRGD diagram
    1013.1.

LANE_LINE — Lane-dividing line on motorway or dual-carriageway
    (broken pattern, typically 100mm with reflective studs).
    TSRGD diagram 1004.

The five line types span the genuinely-different UK commercial
decisions a QS would face when pricing a road-marking tender.

Painted-area marking type per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 9 and various
diagram-numbered references. The area cost driver is paint/
thermoplastic coverage (m² of painted surface).

HATCHED_CHEVRON — Hatched chevron area between carriageways,
    typically at 45° hatching with bordered edges. TSRGD Schedule 9.
GHOST_ISLAND    — Painted refuge area within carriageway, hatched
    border. Common at minor-road junctions and right-turn lanes.
BOX_JUNCTION    — Yellow box junction (cross-hatched, anti-grid-
    locking). TSRGD diagram 1043.
CYCLE_BOX       — Cycle-box / advanced stop line area, typically
    green-coloured surface plus cycle symbol. TSRGD diagram 1001.2.
BUS_STOP_BOX    — Bus stop cage marking (painted bus-stop bay
    outline + BUS legend). TSRGD diagram 1025.
KEEP_CLEAR      — KEEP CLEAR rectangular zone prohibiting waiting
    and parking. TSRGD diagram 1026.

Painted symbol/legend type. UK practice enumerates per occurrence
regardless of physical size (a STOP word is 1nr whether the
characters are 1.6m or 2.8m).

ARROW              — Directional arrow per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 7.
WORD               — Word/legend (BUS, KEEP CLEAR, SLOW, SCHOOL,
                     STOP, GIVE WAY) per TSRGD Schedule 8.
GIVE_WAY_TRIANGLE  — Give-way triangle marking per TSRGD diagram 1023.
TRANSVERSE_BAR     — Transverse bar pair per TSRGD Schedule 6 (the
                     transverse element of give-way / stop lines).
MINI_ROUNDABOUT    — Mini-roundabout central symbol per TSRGD
                     diagram 1003.4.
CYCLE_SYMBOL       — Cycle symbol per TSRGD diagram 1057 (painted
                     cycle icon on cycle lane or shared surface).

Reflective road stud type per BS EN 1463-1.

NON_DEPRESSIBLE — Older specification adhered or mechanically fixed,
    still common on minor roads and lower-volume routes. Not
    snowplough-resistant.
DEPRESSIBLE     — Motorway / dual-carriageway specification per
    BS EN 1463-1 Class TRP-D. Stud body retracts into the running
    surface under snowplough blade pressure.
BIDIRECTIONAL   — Two-way visibility stud for junction approaches
    and central reserves.

Reflective road stud colour per TSRGD 2016.

WHITE — Lane lines (lane-dividing studs on motorway lane separators).
RED   — Left edge of carriageway (UK left-hand drive convention).
AMBER — Right edge / central reserve / motorway hard shoulder line.
GREEN — Lay-by / slip-road indication.
BLUE  — Emergency / fire-hydrant marking.

marking_material.description:
Road marking material per SHW Cl. 1208.

THERMOPLASTIC   — Hot-applied thermoplastic (dominant UK material;
                  4-7 year life on highway routes).
COLD_PAINT      — Cold-applied paint per BS EN 1871 (lower-cost,
                  1-2 year life, common for car parks and minor
                  installations).
PREFORMED_TAPE  — Preformed retroreflective tape; specialist
                  applications (temporary diversions, premium-
                  retroreflective requirements).
MMA             — Methyl methacrylate cold-applied two-pack resin;
                  high-friction, high-durability, premium cost.

Material is carried on the description text only per UK QS practice
(NOT a structural discriminator and NOT a banding axis). Material
differences are priced as part of the per-line-width rate rather
than as separate bill lines.

tools.title: Compute Traffic Sign BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Traffic sign installation per SHW Cl. 1201-1206 and TSRGD 2016. Discriminates between five TSRGD sign classifications via the sign_type enum: warning triangular, regulatory circular, regulatory rectangular, directional rectangular, and information rectangular. SECOND member of the highway L1 leaf (after S36 VRS) and FIRST member of the highway_signs_markings L2 leaf — 41st assembly. Five variant presets cover the principal UK commercial scenarios: rural warning triangle on single post, urban regulatory circular, rural advance directional on twin posts, motorway gantry ADS, and urban information rectangle. Routes via three new WorkCategory entries (TRAFFIC_SIGN_POST, TRAFFIC_SIGN_FACE, SIGN_FOUNDATION). Codes: CESMM4 X.4 (Class X §4 — traffic signs), NRM2 34.8 (Site works — signs), MMHW 1300.1.{a}.{h} (Series 1300 — Road Lighting/Traffic Signs/Bollards, with 2D banding by face_area × mounting_height), SMM7 Q40.6 (Section Q40 — Fencing/site furniture). 25th use of classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern; 6th use of declared-then-banded AND the SECOND 2D-banded handler (MMHW 1300.1.{a}.{h} bands by both axes simultaneously). Example params: post_length_m=3 m (1.5–12), post_count=1 Nr (1–4), faces=1 Nr (1–6). Example call: {"params": {"post_length_m": 3, "post_count": 1, "faces": 1}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Parameters for a single traffic sign installation.

Geometry interpretation:
  - ``post_length_m`` is the length of the supporting post above
    ground (UK convention measures the *above-ground* length, not
    the often-greater driven/embedded length). For gantry signs,
    this is the height of each gantry leg.
  - ``post_count`` is the number of supporting posts. Typical
    values: 1 (small warning/regulatory), 2 (twin-post directional,
    gantry legs).
  - ``faces`` is the number of distinct sign faces on the
    assembly. A single gantry can carry 1-3 distinct sign faces
    (one per lane); a twin-post directional can carry advance
    and confirmation faces.

Face geometry:
  - ``actual_face_area_m2`` is the m² of a single face (used for
    face-area descriptions; the WorkItem quantity is enumerated
    per face).

Foundation:
  - ``foundation_type`` carries the SHW Cl. 1204 classification.
  - ``concrete_grade`` is for description text — concrete is
    deemed-included in the foundation unit rate (no separate
    CONCRETE line emitted).
  - ``approximate_foundation_volume_m3`` is for description text
    only — UK QS convention does not measure sign-foundation
    concrete separately (see SHW Cl. 1204).

sign_type.description:
Traffic sign type per TSRGD 2016 classification.

WARNING_TRIANGULAR — Warning sign per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 2.
    Equilateral triangular face (typically 750mm/900mm/1200mm
    per side per TSM Ch. 4). Red border on white background;
    warning of hazards ahead. The dominant low-cost UK case.

REGULATORY_CIRCULAR — Regulatory sign per TSRGD 2016 Schedule 3.
    Circular face (typically 600mm/750mm/900mm diameter).
    Red border (prohibition) or blue (mandatory). The
    dominant UK enumerated-regulatory case.

REGULATORY_RECTANGULAR — Regulatory sign per TSRGD 2016
    Schedules 3 and 4. Rectangular face — used for parking
    restrictions, speed limits with supplementary plates,
    loading bays. White background with text/symbols.

DIRECTIONAL_RECTANGULAR — Directional sign per TSRGD 2016
    Schedule 11. Rectangular face — large area for route
    legends. Green (primary routes), blue (motorways), white
    (local). Internally illuminated where specified per
    TSM Ch. 7.

INFORMATION_RECTANGULAR — Information sign per TSRGD 2016
    Schedule 12. Rectangular face — tourist destinations,
    facilities, services, place names.

The five sign types span the genuinely-different UK commercial
decisions a QS would face when pricing a traffic-sign tender.

face_area_class.description:
Sign face area band per UK QS pricing practice. The face area
drives material cost (retroreflective sheeting per m²),
fabrication cost, and (above the small threshold) typically
drives the number of posts required. Bands chosen to match
typical UK signage practice per TSM Ch. 4:

SMALL       — ≤0.5m² (typical warning triangle 900mm side)
MEDIUM      — 0.5-2.0m² (typical regulatory 750-900mm dia,
              small directional plate)
LARGE       — 2.0-10.0m² (typical single-route directional
              on twin posts)

              multiple lanes; sometimes called "gantry"
              face area class)

mounting_height_class.description:
Sign mounting height band per UK QS pricing practice. The
mounting height drives access cost (small post = step-ladder;
elevated = MEWP / cherry picker; gantry = full lane closure +
specialist lifting). Bands chosen to match typical UK access
practice:

POST_MOUNTED — <3m AGL (above ground level) — typical for
               warning and regulatory signs on single posts.
               Hand-tool access from the verge.
ELEVATED     — 3-5m AGL — typical for large directional signs
               on twin posts. MEWP / cherry-picker access.
GANTRY       — >5m AGL — overhead gantry signs spanning
               carriageway. Lane-closure + specialist lifting
               required.

foundation_type.description:
Sign foundation type per SHW Cl. 1204. Drives the SIGN_FOUNDATION
description and the implicit unit rate the QS will apply.

POST_MOUNTED_SMALL  — Small mass-concrete block (~0.3m³) for a
    single warning or regulatory sign on a single post. The
    dominant UK case by count.
POST_MOUNTED_LARGE  — Larger mass-concrete block (~0.6m³) for
    a heavier sign or longer post (>3m post height).
TWIN_POST_PAD       — Pair of small mass-concrete blocks linked
    by a ground beam for a twin-post directional sign.
GANTRY_PAD          — Full reinforced pad (~2m³+) for gantry
    legs. Concrete is still deemed-included in the unit rate
    per SHW Cl. 1205 — the gantry pad is bundled with gantry
    leg supply.

post_material.description:
Sign post material per SHW Cl. 1201. UK convention specifies
hot-dip galvanised steel as the default; aluminium is used for
lightweight applications; timber is exceptional (heritage
locations only).

anyOf.description:
Schema § 1.1 — the typed payload returned inside `MCPResponse[ComputeResult]`.

Free-tier responses omit `drawings` (the downloadable CAD artefact
pointers — the paid differentiator); the bridge enforces this. The
`audit_trail` and the inline `drawing` preview are present on BOTH tiers
(V1 ALIGN / 60th-fire D + C). `text_summary` is bounded to 2000 chars —
keeps the LLM-facing summary token-cheap and forces longer narrative into
BoQ row descriptions where it belongs. `warnings` is the non-fatal
geometry advisory list (both tiers).

parameters_used.description:
Schema § 1.2 — the parameter snapshot the engine actually used.

Splits user-supplied values from engine defaults so customers can see
which numbers came from them and which the engine filled in. Every
defaulted parameter SHOULD have a corresponding entry in `assumptions`
— the bridge layer enforces this when wrapping engine output.

items.description:
Schema § 1.3 — a single bill row in the requested standard's format.

`description` is the non-verbatim functional description per spec § 13.9 /
§ 15 invariant — NEVER reproduces a standard's verbatim clause text.
`rate` / `amount` ship null because rates are commodity data the customer
owns; the engine's job is the measurement, not the pricing.

totals_summary.description:
Schema § 1.4 — totals_summary as a typed wrapper around the free-form dict.

Wire shape is a flat object (`{"concrete_m3": {...}, "rebar_t": {...}}`).
We model it as `RootModel`-equivalent via `model_config(extra="allow")`
+ a single `__root__`-style `entries` dict. Pydantic v2 recommends
`RootModel` for free-form roots; using a wrapper class keeps the import
surface uniform with the rest of this module.

anyOf.description:
Schema § 1.6a — inline server-rendered SVG preview of the geometry.

The MCP mirror of the web ``/compute`` response's ``drawing`` field
(``api.schemas.compute.DrawingRef``): the same on-screen dimensioned
drawing both tiers see in the workspace, surfaced on the MCP compute
response so a chat client can render it inline (60th-fire item C). This
is the on-screen preview — present on BOTH tiers per the free/paid
boundary; the downloadable CAD artefacts (DXF / dimensioned PDF) remain
the paid differentiator via the export tools.

Defined here rather than importing ``DrawingRef`` because the web
``schemas`` package imports back into this module (``schemas.render``),
so reusing it would create an import cycle — the MCP wire contract keeps
its own copy, the same pattern as ``BoQRow`` / ``DrawingReference``.

items.description:
Schema § 1.6 — paid-tier drawing artefact pointer.

`url` is an R2-signed URL; expiry is carried in `_meta.deliverables.expires_at`
on the envelope (not duplicated here). `layers` is DXF-only; PDF/SVG
callers omit it.

Schema § 1.7 — paid-tier audit-trail entry.

One entry per BoQ row; `boq_row_index` ties to the row position in
`ComputeResult.boq_rows`. `derivation` is the human-readable formula
walk-through; `formula` is the optional formal expression.

Schema § 1.8 — a non-fatal geometry advisory (56th-fire T2).

The wire projection of the engine's `core.GeometryWarning`. Advisory only:
a warning NEVER changes a measured quantity — it flags geometry that is
valid but likely a mistake (e.g. a stale dependent-height default). Present
on BOTH tiers — a correctness/safety signal, not a paid feature.

tools.name: compute_flexible_pavement
tools.title: Compute Flexible (Bituminous) Pavement Build-Up BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Flexible pavement build-up: optional capping (Class 6F) + Type 1 (Class 1A) granular sub-base + asphalt concrete base (AC) + binder course (AC/HRA) + optional tack coat + surface course (AC/HRA/SMA/TSCS). Routes the bound layers through PAVEMENT_BASE/BINDER/SURFACE handlers with pavement_family discrimination across all four standards. Sub-base and capping route through the v8 FILL_SUB_BASE/FILL_CAPPING SHW-class-aware handlers. Four traffic-category defaults (domestic/light/medium/heavy) per DMRB CD 226. All four standards render (CESMM4 R.1-R.4, NRM2 34.4-34.6, MMHW 700, SMM7 Q20+Q22). Example params: length=100 m (0.5–2000), width=6 m (0.5–30), sub_base_thickness_mm=150 mm (100–500). Example call: {"params": {"length": 100, "width": 6, "sub_base_thickness_mm": 150}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Input parameters for a flexible pavement assembly.

Geometric defaults match a 100m × 6m urban access road (medium
traffic) per DMRB CD 226 starting build-up: 150mm Type 1 sub-base,
150mm AC 32 base, 60mm AC 20 binder, 40mm SMA 10 surface.

traffic_category.description:
Coarse traffic category for QS-level pavement build-up defaults.

Maps to typical DMRB CD 226 design traffic ranges:
  DOMESTIC ≈ < 0.3 msa     (driveways, courtyards)
  LIGHT    ≈ 0.3–2.5 msa   (estate roads, footways w/ vehicle access)
  MEDIUM   ≈ 2.5–10 msa    (urban access, minor distributors)
  HEAVY    ≈ 10–30 msa     (urban distributors, light industrial)

For design traffic > 30 msa or > category 4 subgrade, a full pavement
design per DMRB CD 226 is required and the parametric defaults here
are not sufficient — the user must specify thicknesses and materials
explicitly.

tools.name: compute_permeable_pavement
tools.title: Compute Permeable Pavement (CIRIA C753 SuDS) BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Permeable pavement build-up per CIRIA C753 — The SuDS Manual Chapter 20. Covers the three principal UK permeable surface types (Permeable Block Paving per BS 7533-13; Porous Asphalt per SHW Cl. 938; Porous no-fines Concrete per CIRIA C753) and the three CIRIA infiltration regimes (System A full infiltration; System B partial / sides-tanked; System C no infiltration / fully tanked). Emits excavation + formation prep + tanking liner (Systems B/C) + geotextile separator + Class 3 open-graded reservoir sub-base + laying course (PBP) + permeable surface + perforated outlet pipe (Systems B/C) + disposal. Routes the reservoir sub-base, the tanking liner, and the permeable surface through three parallel classed-then-legacy discriminators (is_reservoir_sub_base, is_pavement_tanking, pavement_family) across all four standards. SMM7 PBP routes to Q25 (block pavings — different trade) while PA/PC stay at Q22 (asphalt trade) — UK trade-boundary platform principle. First launch-class assembly built entirely on existing WorkCategory vocabulary. Example params: length=12 m (0.5–500), width=5 m (0.5–100), reservoir_thickness_mm=350 mm (150–1000). Example call: {"params": {"length": 12, "width": 5, "reservoir_thickness_mm": 350}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Input parameters for a permeable pavement assembly.

Geometric defaults match a 12m × 5m residential drive with PBP
surface and System A (full infiltration) — the dominant UK
small-civils SuDS use case.

surface_type.description:
Three principal UK permeable surface types per CIRIA C753.
Mapped 1:1 onto the new PavementFamily enum extensions (PBP/PA/PC).
Carried as a dedicated enum on Parameters so the assembly
parametrisation expresses intent in CIRIA-Manual vocabulary.

infiltration_system.description:
Three CIRIA C753 (SuDS Manual Ch.20) permeable-pavement infiltration
regimes. Drives the membrane / outlet pipe inclusion.

tools.name: compute_rigid_pavement
tools.title: Compute Rigid (Concrete) Pavement Build-Up BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_end_area_earthworks. Rigid pavement build-up: optional capping (Class 6F) + Type 1 (Class 1A) granular sub-base + optional separation membrane + PQC slab (URC, JRC, or CRCP variant) with joint formwork (transverse contraction, longitudinal construction, expansion) and reinforcement (dowel bars + tie bars + optional fabric mesh for JRC, continuous longitudinal for CRCP). Routes the slab and its joints/reinforcement through the v12 is_pavement_slab discrimination to pavement-specific codes across all four standards (CESMM4 Class R, NRM2 Group 34.7, MMHW Series 1000, SMM7 Q21). Sub-base and capping route through the v8 FILL_SUB_BASE/FILL_CAPPING SHW-class-aware handlers. Three pavement-type defaults (URC/JRC/CRCP) per DMRB CD 226. Reinforcement scheduled per BS 8666:2020 (shape 00 dowels and tie bars; mass-only mesh and CRCP continuous). Example params: length=50 m (0.5–2000), width=7 m (0.5–30), sub_base_thickness_mm=150 mm (100–500). Example call: {"params": {"length": 50, "width": 7, "sub_base_thickness_mm": 150}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

params.description:
Input parameters for a rigid pavement assembly.

Defaults: 50m × 7m urban distributor — JRC with 25m bay length, 230mm
slab on 150mm Type 1 sub-base, A393 mesh mid-depth. Tie bars at

pavement_type.description:
Named UK rigid pavement variants per DMRB CD 226 / HD 26.

URC  : Unreinforced Concrete (jointed, no mesh, dowels + tie bars only)
JRC  : Jointed Reinforced Concrete (mesh mid-depth, dowels + tie bars)
CRCP : Continuously Reinforced Concrete Pavement (continuous longitudinal
       steel, no transverse joints)

anyOf.description:

tools.name: compute_anchored_wall
tools.title: Compute Anchored Retaining Wall BoQ
tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_cantilever_wall. Anchored retaining wall — the only wall family member that pre-stresses the retained soil mass into the wall via post-tensioned ground anchors per BS EN 1537. Three structural variants: in-situ reinforced concrete (INSITU_RC, economic 5-10m); steel king-post-and-lagging (KING_POST, typical 4-8m, often temporary); driven sheet pile (SHEET_PILED, quays/cofferdams/deep basements). Eight VARIANT_PRESETS exercise the 'one parameter form, eight variants, four standards' moat #1 claim across all three structural variants. The in-situ RC body routes via wall_type='anchored' attribute discrimination: CESMM4 F.6.4, NRM2 11.3.4, MMHW 1700.4.3 (SHW Cl. 1709/1710), SMM7 E10.3.3. Ground anchors and stressing route to new specialist handlers (CESMM4 Class C; NRM2 Group 7; MMHW Series 1600; SMM7 D32). King-post sections to CESMM4 P.5 / NRM2 7.3 / MMHW 1600.3 / SMM7 D32; sheet piles to CESMM4 P.4 / NRM2 7.4 / MMHW 1600.4 / SMM7 D31; timber lagging to CESMM4 O.3 / NRM2 16.4 / MMHW 2500.7 / SMM7 G20.1. Example params: stem_height=6 m (2–15), stem_thickness=0.5 m (0–1.5), wall_length=25 m (5–200). Example call: {"params": {"stem_height": 6, "stem_thickness": 0.5, "wall_length": 25}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier). Pass `freeboard` (clearance below the wall top, m) instead of the retained-height field to set the retained fill by clearance — the engine back-calculates it as stem − freeboard. Supplying both is rejected.

params.description:
Parameter form for an anchored retaining wall.

A single dataclass that — through combinations of its fields and the
``wall_form`` discriminator — produces all eight VARIANT_PRESETS plus
arbitrary user-specified geometries across all three structural
variants (INSITU_RC, KING_POST, SHEET_PILED). Sensible defaults
yield a 6m in-situ RC wall with a single row of permanent anchors.

wall_form.description:
Structural form of the anchored retaining wall.

INSITU_RC   — Continuous in-situ reinforced concrete stem with a
              continuous waling beam (typically at the wall head;
              multi-row anchored walls have a waling at each anchor
              level). Anchors penetrate the stem and are stressed
              against the waling. Routes the stem to CESMM4 F.6.4 /
              NRM2 11.3.4 / MMHW 1700.4.3 / SMM7 E10.3.3.

KING_POST   — Steel H-section (UC or UB) "king posts" or "soldier
              piles" driven or socketed at regular centres
              (typically 2.0-3.0 m c/c), with horizontal timber
              or precast concrete lagging panels between. A
              continuous RC waling beam runs at the head (and at
              each anchor row if multi-row) transferring the anchor
              loads to the king posts. King posts → CESMM4 P.5 /
              NRM2 7.3 / MMHW 1600.3 / SMM7 D32. Lagging →
              CESMM4 O.3 (timber) or F.6.4 (precast concrete) /
              NRM2 16.4 (timber) or 13 (precast) / MMHW 2500.7
              (timber) or 1700.4.3 (precast) / SMM7 G20.1 (timber)
              or E50 (precast).

SHEET_PILED — Driven steel sheet piles (Larssen LX, AZ, GU
              profiles) forming a continuous wall, with a
              continuous RC waling at the head. Sheet pile toe
              drives below the excavation formation to provide
              passive resistance; anchor loads at the head are
              restrained back. Sheet piles → CESMM4 P.4 /
              NRM2 7.4 / MMHW 1600.4 / SMM7 D31.

anchor_permanence.description:
Permanent or temporary anchor classification per BS EN 1537.

PERMANENT — Design life >= 2 years; tendons require double
            corrosion protection (DCP) per BS EN 1537 Table 1.
            Stressing forces locked off and retained for life.
TEMPORARY — Design life < 2 years (typically supporting basement
            excavation until permanent structure is built).
            Single corrosion protection (SCP) acceptable.
            Often de-stressed and tendons cropped on completion.

anchor_corrosion_protection.description:
Anchor corrosion protection level per BS EN 1537.

SINGLE — Grease-and-sheath protection of free length;
         grouted-only fixed length. Acceptable for temporary
         anchors and benign permanent environments.
DOUBLE — Grease-and-sheath PLUS a continuous corrugated plastic
         duct over the full free length, AND a corrugated duct
         over the fixed length. Mandatory for permanent anchors
         in aggressive ground per BS EN 1537 Table 1.

lagging_type.description:
For KING_POST variant: timber or precast concrete lagging.

TIMBER         — Horizontal timber boards (C24 or similar) between
                 king-post flanges. Lower cost; permitted only for
                 temporary works and certain permanent applications
                 where durability allows (creosote treatment etc.).
PRECAST_CONC   — Precast concrete lagging panels between king-post
                 flanges. Used for permanent works where timber
                 is not acceptable. More expensive than timber.

Only relevant when wall_form == KING_POST. Ignored otherwise.

excavation_support.description:
Excavation support strategy for below-ground assemblies.

Consumed by retaining walls (cantilever, gravity, counterfort,
anchored, bored pile), foundation assemblies, and drainage chambers
that involve a battered or vertical-supported pit. The enum value is
surfaced in the description text of the relevant excavation BoQ line
and in some standards (CESMM4 E.4.4 et seq.) drives a separate code.

tools.description: Paid tier only. Calling this without an authenticated CivilQuants account returns TIER_INSUFFICIENT — sign up at https://civilquants.com/pricing or use the free-tier alternative compute_cantilever_wall. Cast-in-place bored concrete pile retaining wall, the SEVENTH member of the wall family and the FIFTH of the retaining_walls L1 leaf. The SIXTH structural system in the retaining / earth-structures domain (after mass concrete / RC / steel / mesh-and-stone / reinforced-soil-with-facing). Four structural forms via the bored_pile_form discriminator: CONTIGUOUS (clear-spaced piles, shotcrete face), SECANT_HARD_SOFT (alternating soft/hard overlapping piles, intermediate watertightness), SECANT_HARD_HARD (overlapping RC piles, maximum watertightness; deep basements), and KING_POST_AND_LAGGING_RC (widely-spaced RC king posts with lagging panels). 18th use of the classed-then-legacy attribute discrimination pattern, applied via the CONCRETE_REINFORCED handler's new wall_type='bored_pile' branch for the capping beam (when included). Routes via five new WorkCategory entries (BORED_PILE_CONCRETE, BORED_PILE_BORE, BORED_PILE_NR, BORED_PILE_HEAD_PREP, BORED_PILE_INTERLOCK) covering the CESMM4 Class P §P.8 three-line cast-in-place pile measurement convention plus the Class Q ancillaries head-prep line and the secant-specific interlock line. Codes: CESMM4 P.8.1-4 + Q.1.1, NRM2 7.6.1-4 + 7.5.1, MMHW 1600.5-6 (SHW Cl. 1602/1603), and SMM7 D30.1-5 — D30 (Cast in place piling) is OPENED at this session as the conventional UK QS named home. Capping beam routes via CONCRETE_REINFORCED with wall_type='bored_pile' to F.6.5 / 11.3.5 / 1700.4.4 / E10.3.4. Reinforcement billed itemised (separate audit line per BS 8666:2020 cage) on top of the pile rate by S31 decision. Eight variant presets exercise all four BoredPileForm values (2/2/2/2 split). Example params: wall_length_m=20 m (5–200), retained_height_m=6 m (2–20), embedment_below_formation_m=4 m (1–15). Example call: {"params": {"wall_length_m": 20, "retained_height_m": 6, "embedment_below_formation_m": 4}, "standard": "MMHW"}. Omitted parameters use sensible engineering defaults. Pass deliverables=["xlsx","dxf","pdf"] (any subset) to also receive one-shot download URLs in the same call: Excel BoQ (both tiers, watermarked free) plus the dimensioned DXF (CAD) and PDF drawing sheets (paid tier).

tools.description: Free tier. Renders the MMHW standard only — CESMM4, NRM2 and SMM7 require a paid tier. Anonymous callers welcome.
